question: to the Commission Jan Farský (PPE) Subject:

Since the activation of the Temporary Protection Directive, millions of Ukrainian refugees have gained access to the labour market in the European Union. However, according to a recent analysis by the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, survey data show that 57 % of Ukrainian refugees in Europe are employed, which is a gap of 22 percentage points compared with nationals of the host countries. A serious problem remains the structural mismatch between qualifications and the jobs performed. Up to 60 % of Ukrainian refugees work below their qualification level, while those with tertiary education are five times more likely to hold low-skilled positions than local workers. This leads to significant wage gaps and at the same time limits the ability of host economies to use the available human capital and therefore also limits the potential increase in GDP, which is estimated at up to 0.7 percentage points per year. Does the Commission plan to propose additional targeted measures to prevent long-term exclusion from the labour market and skills degradation among Ukrainian refugees, especially in sectors facing persistent labour shortages?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.6.2026) The Commission Recommendation on the recognition of qualifications for people fleeing Russia’s invasion of Ukraine1 was adopted to ensure the swift integration of beneficiaries of temporary protection in the EU labour market. It provides guidance to Member States on the quick and fair recognition of qualifications so that professionals enjoying temporary protection can access jobs that match their potential. The Commission launched the EU Talent Pool Pilot2 for beneficiaries of temporary protection, available in Ukrainian and Russian language, to help match jobseekers benefitting from temporary protection with vacancies from EU employers. Beneficiaries of temporary protection have shown faster labour market integration rates than those of other refugee groups3. The Commission is exploring the potential of common rules to simplify the qualification recognition procedures for third-country nationals4, in order to better harness their human capital in the EU. The Erasmus+ programme has also been mobilised to contribute supporting the skills of Ukrainian pupils, students, young people and educators. The recently adopted EU Anti-Poverty Strategy5 announced the launch of the first-stage consultation of European social partners on the possible direction of EU action to support the activation of people excluded from the labour market.
1 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2022/554 of 5 April 2022 on the recognition of qualifications for people
